description:
California Air Resources Board (CARB) proposed Clean Space and Water Heater Standards (December 2025 proposal, not yet adopted). Each manufacturer's annual GHG-emissive space and water heater sales in California (equipment <= 2,000,000 Btu/hr) may not exceed a share of its total annual sales: space heating 40% (2030), 33% (2035), 25% (2040+); water heating 60% (2030), 55% (2035), 50% (2040+). Applicable fraction = 1 - emissive sales limit (space heating 60%, 67%, 75%; water heating 40%, 45%, 50%), entered as cumulative fractions by start year (rows that share a jurisdiction are stages of one policy, so the stage with the latest start year replaces the earlier ones). Pool heating is not covered because gas pool heating is not broken out in Scout. See slides 'Proposed GHG-Emissive Sales Limit' and 'Proposed Statewide GHG-Emissive Equipment Sales Limits'.

https://www.bayren.org/sites/default/files/documents/2026/3_maggie_seay_california_air_resources_board.pdf
fraction notes: Gross statewide target. Reference local programs in CA (BAAQMD zero-NOx rules and SCAQMD boiler rules) are typed 'local' and already count toward it: for each segment and year the model uses the larger of this target and the summed local shares, so nothing is entered net of them here. For example, natural gas heating in single family and mobile homes is max(0.60, 0.313) = 0.60 in 2030, and new multifamily boilers stay at the 0.643 local total (0.354 BAAQMD + 0.289 SCAQMD) until the 0.67 stage of 2035. Replaces the earlier rows that were entered net of the local shares (e.g., 0.287/0.357/0.437 for single family heating). Updated 2026-10 (type column): policy-derived fraction (1 minus the emissive sales limit), not a ComStock/ResStock energy share; applied to the state's full segment, assuming sales share equals energy share and ignoring stock-turnover timing.

description:
The CO Clean Heat Standard requires gas distribution utilities to cut emissions by 4% by 2025 and by 22% by 2030, with more ambitious cuts to come in later years. Under the CO Clean Heat Standard, those utilities are required to develop cost-effective plans that will achieve meaningful reductions in the emissions that result from delivering fuel to homes and businesses. These plans will then be evaluated by the Colorado Public Utilities Commission.

https://leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/2021a_264_signed.pdf
fraction notes: Updated 2026-10: policy target (percent emissions reduction by gas distribution utilities), not a geographic energy share, so it is not recomputed. Assumption: applied to all fossil heating in CO residential and commercial buildings; natural gas is ~94% of CO fossil site energy (ComStock + ResStock baseline; ComStock 97%, ResStock 94%), so the effective share on gas utility customers alone would be ~0.208 for the 0.22 stage. 0.22 is kept to preserve the layering with the CARB-modeled CO rows.
